title: Rani Sada Kaur
hookLine: a widow who led the Kanhaiya misl and backed her young son-in-law, Ranjit

lines: HER HUSBAND KILLED BY THE OTHER SIDE.
cards: A betrothal between two families lately at war: that's where today begins.

In one of the quarrels between the misls, Sikh histories say, Gurbakhsh Singh, son and heir of Jai Singh of the Kanhaiya misl, was killed in battle against a coalition that included the Sukerchakia misl.
His widow was left with a young daughter, a grieving father-in-law and a band of riders. You met her earlier in this block. Her name was Sada Kaur.

teach.h: A FEUD TURNED INTO A MARRIAGE.
teach.b: The Sukerchakia chief, Maha Singh, had a son named Ranjit. Sikh histories say Sada Kaur's daughter, Mehtab Kaur, was betrothed to that boy. Her daughter was promised to the son of the chief her husband had died fighting.
Some tellings credit the old chief Jai Singh with the match; in the histories, Sada Kaur is the one who made it work. A marriage turned a feud into a family.
That's the first thing to see in her: she could put grief to work for peace. The second is what she did with her place.
Day eight hundred ninety-one met her at the head of the Kanhaiya band, commanding its riders and managing its lands.
She used that place not to settle the score, but to build something with the family on the other side of it. The third is today's line.
Ranjit was young, with older, stronger chiefs all around him. Sada Kaur put her men and her judgment behind her son-in-law.
When he moved, the histories say, her riders often moved with him, and her counsel went too; they give her a large part in his rise.
The story doesn't stay sweet: later the two would fall out, and that comes in its own time.
But at the start, when the boy had a name and not much else, a woman who had lost her husband in a feud with his family chose to stand behind him anyway.

how: Sikh histories remember Rani Sada Kaur as a leader of the Kanhaiya misl and as the ally behind the young Ranjit Singh.

games.q: you're Sada Kaur. your husband has been killed fighting a coalition that included the Sukerchakia misl. their chief has a young son. what do you do?
o: swear a feud against the Sukerchakia forever.
join your daughter to their son, and back him.
give up the misl and leave.
games.why: her daughter Mehtab Kaur was betrothed to Ranjit, and Sada Kaur put her riders and her counsel behind him.

practice: Bring to mind a young person in your life, a niece, a student, a new hire, your own kid, and what they're trying that's a little bigger than they are.
Think what you could put behind them, not unasked advice but something real, your time, a ride, a word to the right person, a seat at your table; if you pray, say Waheguru on each breath out.
